body:
Ok I did some testing and it seems all scripts save regardless of what save shortcut is pressed, my default shortcut for saving all scripts is Alt+Shift+S  but just pressing Ctrl+S saves them all anyway.
 
Try changing your save all scripts shortcut back to its default and leave the save all scenes as is and see if that works, using my default for saving all scenes also saved the scripts and worked with the script editor in focus.

Please see this thread because I wasn't the only one that gets this issue.
https://forum.godotengine.org/t/shortcuts-dont-work/137760/5

Edit: Yes, it works when the default Ctrl+Shift+Alt+S is used. Everything is saved normally. As soon as I change the shortcut keys to Ctrl+S it breaks, but it only breaks when the script editor has focus. That shouldn't be happening.
Try changing the save all scripts shortcut to something else, then set save all scenes to Ctrl+S. The script editor shortcut most likely has priority over other shortcuts when in focus.

I tested this, and all the default key presses work. However, if you change the alternatives to BOTH **Save All Scripts** and **Save All Scenes** to be the **same** shortcut, neither works. Seems like that's the specific bug.

> Try changing the save all scripts shortcut to something else, then set save all scenes to Ctrl+S. The script editor shortcut most likely has priority over other shortcuts when in focus.

The last video I recorded was corrupted. I am going to try and find time to make another tonight with the recommendations posted here. I already know they work when the keys are different. If both keys are set to the same it doesn't work, but only when the script editor has focus. It the editor has some priority then than seems odd because it allows both keys to be set the same then someone would expect it to work with both keys regardless of what window had focus. 

I'll update later if I get the video created.

That isn't necessarily a bug, though the intended behaviour might be confusing. 

It works when save all scenes is set to Ctrl+S, save all scripts remain as Alt+Ctrl+S and save scene is no longer set to Ctrl+S (at least in my testing only the selected scene saved when both save all scenes and save scene were set to Ctrl+S). 

Some documentation might be better than trying to change the behaviour, as it might break things we can't think about right now.

I have no idea, but maybe someone can provide some confirmation on it, because it's odd that if you leave the shortcuts to default settings, this does **not** happen, even when the script editor has focus, the default shortcut keys still save all scenes. 

- Ctrl+Shift+Alt+S (default) saves all scenes, and all scripts even when the script editor has focus.
- Ctrl+S saves all scenes and all scripts when a scene has focus
- Ctrl+S saves all scripts and **no** scenes when the script editor has focus.

When reassigning the keys then it "breaks" and only starts saving scripts. I'm not sure how that would be intended behavior. Why would it work as expected when using default keys, but stop working (because the editor has priority) when keys are changed.

That's what I'm not understanding.

Well the simple answer is because the keys are not shared. Save all scripts is NOT set to Ctrl+S, even though that saves all scripts and only the selected scene (default behaviour). So when the shortcut is changed, the event no longer propagates when the script editor has focus, because the script editor completely absorbs all of the inputs intended for it.

When a scene is saved, some kind of signal is probably sent that causes the scripts to save as well, but the input won't reach the scene if the script editor has absorbed it. That's why the shortcuts don't overlap. When they do overlap it's all about what gets the input first and what it does with it.

If the script editor gets the input it saves all scripts then marks that input as handled.

If the scene gets the input it saves (one or all) then sends a signal to also save all scripts.

The above is just me theorising based on how the script editor and scene act, I could be wrong about the details but I believe the general idea is correct.

You may be correct and it sounds logical, but then maybe we shouldn't have the ability to assign the same shortcut to more than one place, or as you said before this needs some documentation because even if it is working as intended, its not working as expected. 

It's very confusing that it allows the keys to be set, but then doesn't do what would be expected. For the time being I'll just use different keys for scripts and scenes, but would like to get some official confirmation as to what the expected behavior is supposed to be in this situation or have it clearer in the documentation.

More than likely your theory is correct, whether intended or not, that it probably what's happening.
This is indeed the result of editor shortcut contexts, which can be quite confusing, the described issue of both failing seems like a bug though, one should take precedence
@dragonforge-dev said they could reproduce the same issue on Windows as well.

@AThousandShips, it's not a bug. I have tested this again just now, here are the results:
### Setup 1:
Save All Scenes: Ctrl+S
Save Scene: Default (Ctrl+S)
Save Script: Default (Alt+Ctrl+S)
Save All Scripts: Default (Alt+Shift+S)

When saving with the script editor in focus, all scripts and the selected scene saves.

### Setup 2:
Save All Scenes: Ctrl+S
Save Scene: Removed or Changed from Default
Save Script: Default (Alt+Ctrl+S)
Save All Scripts: Default (Alt+Shift+S)

When saving with the script editor in focus, all scripts and all scenes save.

### Setup 3:
Save All Scenes: Ctrl+S
Save Scene: Removed or Changed from Default
Save Script: Default (Alt+Ctrl+S)
Save All Scripts: Ctrl+S

When saving with script editor in focus, all scripts and no scenes save.

### Setup 4:
Save All Scenes: Ctrl+S
Save Scene: Default (Ctrl+S)
Save Script: Default (Alt+Ctrl+S)
Save All Scripts: Ctrl+S

When saving with script editor in focus, all scripts and no scenes save.
When scene tree tab is in focus, Save Scene takes precedence over Save All Scenes (see setup 1 and 4). So the selected scene and all scripts are saved.
The order of precedence goes as follows: (This is the general idea)
- Script Editor (when in focus) -> handles shortcut -> Shortcut Operation Triggers -> Input does not propagate
- Script Editor (when in foucs) -> does not handle shortcut -> passes it along -> Scene Tree gets shortcut -> (if Save Scene and Save All Scenes overlap -> Save Scene takes precedence) -> shortcut handled -> Shortcut Operation Triggers -> Save All Scripts Operation does trigger.

The system is working as intended, as I said above, the only thing that might be necessary is some documentation to give users an idea of the heirarcy of the operations the shortcuts trigger, so they have a better idea of where shortcuts are "allowed" and "not allowed" to overlap.

In my opinion there is no need to change anything about how this works. It makes sense or someone to want to save all scripts without saving all scenes (or any scene) but it doesn't make sense for the alternative. A solution could be to warn if those shortcuts  overlap. For example, if Save All Scenes and Save Scene shortcut overlap, Save All Scenes will **never** fire, so a warning there will be nice. The same can be said for Save All Scenes and Save All Scripts, if they overlap and the Script Editor has focus, Save All Scenes will again not fire.

@AThousandShips 

Then this **should** be listed as a bug, because the script editor **shouldn't** work differently under specific conditions. It shouldn't be marking the key as handled and should work the same way the scenes work. There's no need for this overly complicated setup that no one is going to understand.

You are able to change the shortcut keys in the editor, so the shortcut keys should work as expected. In this case, you can change them, but they only work under very specific conditions. If it, for some reason, is intended to work that way, its a very confusing design.

The solution is very simple: 

1. If someone is allowed to reassign the keys to save scripts and scenes, 
2. they should expect those keys to work in the way they are assigned. 

In this case, if its not a bug, they've intentionally designed this so you can reassign keys but then those keys only work under specific situations, which doesn't make any sense to a user who isn't going to understand these special conditions without viewing this thread.

You have a large chain of events happening, but that is not how users are going to think. The process is:

1. I assigned Ctrl+S to save scripts
2. I assigned Ctrl+S to save scenes
3. Ctrl+S will save both scripts and scenes

Not:

1. I assigned Ctrl+S to save everything
2. [insert specific conditions which may prevent this from working]
3. This **will** work when I have a scene targeted
4. This **will not** work when I have script targeted.
5. Why isn't this working????

Godot is stated to be designed to make things easy, and be usable for new/beginning developers. Someone who is new to the engine isn't going to know why this isn't working as expected.

_I am now thinking that adding all this clarification into the documentation is just going to come across as confusing, and the fact that this needs to be clarified in documentation in the first place is a sign that this is more complicated than it needs to be.

The design needs to be fixed so it works as expected, so this extra clarification isn't required in the first place. This is just pushing it off into **"we don't want to fix/change this, so instead, we'll add some extra documentation to state why this doesn't work as a normal user would expect."**_

One goal with basic UI/UX design is that the software should work as expected, otherwise, we end up with **this**, a long thread from a confused user wondering what is going on.

I have spoken with other users who are confused by this as well. @dragonforge-dev stated that they are able to recreate this issue on their end as well, as well as 2 people from discord who were unable to answer why it works this way. 

The fact that this works perfect with the default keys, and only fails when you reassign the keys is more likely **not** working as intended. 

The bottom line is, from a user standpoint, this does not work the way someone would expect it to work.

The editor has scoped keys which is by design, so that part is not a bug

This is part of making Godot usable to make sure there's the ability to configure shortcuts for different places

But this is a broader conversation, but if it does indeed not work with setting both shortcuts to the same value that *is* a bug, but that needs to be evaluated as different people are saying different things

I'll leave it unassessed for now and someone else can help identify it

I remain firmly of the opinion that it is not a bug, if scoped keys are by design, then, for example, the shortcut key to save all scripts  being handled in its scope (saving all script with script editor in focus) and not propagating that key to another scope (scene) is absolutely intended design. 

The relationship between `All Scenes`, `Selected Scene`, and `Script Editor` scopes behave in such a way as to give each the precedence they need within context (focus). Since multiple scenes cannot be selected at the same time, that puts `All Scenes` in last place. 

First and second is determined by who has focus, if `Script Editor` has focus, it is not sharing its scoped keys with `Scene` or `All Scenes`. If `Scene` has focus, it is not sharing its scoped keys with `Script Editor` or `All Scenes`. Saving all scripts when a scene is saved is a design choice, not `Script Editor` sharing input.

If the scoped keys for `Scene`, `All Scenes`, and `Script Editor` overlap, then the one with focus wins. If those keys are not a part of the scope, then it gets passed along until it arrives at a scope where it gets handled and does not propagate further.

I'll end this with a simple multiple choice question: If I set `Save Script` and `Save All Scripts` to the same shortcut, what should occur when that shortcut is pressed?

1. Save All Scripts
2. Save Selected Script
3. Both

As a test, set `Save Scene` and `Save Script` to the same shortcut, modify multiple scripts and the selected scene, with the scene tree in focus, press the save shortcut. You should see that even though the key is set to `Save Script` and **not** `Save All Scripts`, all scripts save anyway, that is because the scene tree is not propagating its input to the script editor, but the scripts are being saved via a different mechanism.

Fixing this "bug" means possibly breaking that behaviour that I will stand on it being better UX than the alternative. If I set all of my shortcuts to Ctrl+S, I absolutely want the program to say NO! and just do what the shortcut is intended to do based on what has precedence, so that precedence is needed. If I set `Save` and `Save All` to the same key, the program should only save, leave the rest untouched. I mean, if I _really_ want all to be saved, I'll set a different shortcut.

@unit-tick if one accepts your "works as designed" argument, the fact of the matter is, you can still do something which got us here to this bug. A user shouldn't have to dig into the code to see why setting shortcuts doesn't work. Also, I can guarantee if nothing is done about it, this is going to get raised again.

I feel like you're arguing about what the solution is. If it works as designed, then perhaps the solution is to not let the user assign the same shortcut to two keys? Or perhaps to make it clearer with a tooltip how **Save Scene** _also_ saves all scripts? Because let's face it, most people aren't going to read the docs before complaining.

I cannot confirm this bug at all, changing the "Save Scene" in the editor shortcuts and the "Save" shortcut in the script editor to a new shortcut and pressing that shortcut the editor saves correctly, saving the script when in the script editor, and the scene when outside it

Now the one thing that is a bit problematic is that it saves all scripts when pressing the shortcut, even when focusing outside the script editor, that is something to discuss as it is unexpected, but might be due to some internal workings that require this

Otherwise things work as expected, at least with respect to the original issue being described

@dragonforge-dev I did not look at the code at all to come to the conclusion I did, it came from strictly testing stuff inside the godot editor. Though I do believe some sort of warning system needs to be put in place, like my `Save Scene` and `Save All Scenes` example, it should be obvious that the shortcut cannot do both, but it would be nice to know which gets precedence and which doesn't.

In conclusion, I agree that documentation and/or an internal warning system would be nice to have.

In some cases a warning makes sense, but in many it makes no sense, and there are already overlapping cases by default, so a warning would be misleading in a big part of cases and would be unhelpful, for example why should the save shortcut have a warning and not, for example, the resume/suspend in the editor and the toggle breakpoint in the script editor, both default bound to `F9`

It's hard to guess what would and what wouldn't be confusing or surprising to any user

That's true. The system is fine as it is from my POV. Sometimes we gotta learn and things working against our understanding isn't always bad design or an oversight, as users we really need to be protected from ourselves sometimes.

But I guess the argument could be that only things within the scope are given warnings when shadowed? But like I stated in my previous comment, it feels obvious enough that only `Save Scene` or `Save All Scene` would work, but everyone will have a different idea of which one should work. So the engine straight up telling them "only this one will work" might be slightly better UX, or just not making it possible for two shortcuts to exist within the same scope, but I feel like that would be harder.

Also "our understanding" is individual, I don't find the scoped context of the shortcuts confusing, quite the opposite, I wouldn't expect the 3D editor to do something when I press a shortcut in the script editor for example, or the scene tree, etc.

Setting both `Save Scene` and `Save All Scenes` to the same shortcut is not on topic for this issue, that should be discussed elsewhere

This issue is specifically about shortcuts in *two different* scopes
True, but I was just also stating the limitation of my agreement to the warning system I "proposed". Didn't intend to get off topic.
